DK28.0 is a specific medical diagnosis code representing an acute gastrointestinal ulcer with bleeding. Within the Danish healthcare system's quality monitoring frameworks, specifically the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this code plays a critical role in tracking patient safety and treatment complications.

Specifically, DK28.0 is utilized as part of a broader set of diagnostic codes to measure the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding) among patients being treated for [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1] [^src3]. Because patients with atrial fibrillation are frequently prescribed anticoagulant medications, monitoring severe bleeding events—including gastrointestinal, intracranial, and other major bleeds—is a vital quality indicator for assessing the safety and efficacy of their clinical management [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].

To capture the full scope of severe bleeding incidents, the AFDK methodology employs a comprehensive list of ICD-10-DK codes. Alongside DK28.0, the indicator for severe bleeding incorporates codes for intracranial bleeding (such as [[di60|DI60]], [[di61|DI61]], [[di62|DI62]], [[ds064|DS064]], [[ds065|DS065]], and [[ds066|DS066]]), a wide array of gastrointestinal bleeding codes (including [[dk25-0|DK25.0]], [[dk25-2|DK25.2]], [[dk25-4|DK25.4]], [[dk25-6|DK25.6]], [[dk26-0|DK26.0]], [[dk26-2|DK26.2]], [[dk26-4|DK26.4]], [[dk26-6|DK26.6]], [[dk27-0|DK27.0]], [[dk27-2|DK27.2]], [[dk27-4|DK27.4]], [[dk27-6|DK27.6]], [[dk28-2|DK28.2]], [[dk28-4|DK28.4]], [[dk28-6|DK28.6]], [[dk29-0|DK29.0]], [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]], [[dk92-0|DK92.0]], [[dk92-1|DK92.1]], and [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]), as well as codes for urinary and respiratory tract bleeding (such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. By standardizing these codes across incident and prevalent patient populations, the RKKP ensures consistent data collection and regional comparison of cardiovascular care quality in Denmark [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].
